BiblicalUsage: Guilty is the word Joseph's brothers use when they remember the pit, and the word the wise woman of Tekoa turns back on David. They say we are verily guilty concerning our brother, in that we saw the anguish of his soul; the woman says the king is as one which is faulty, in that he does not fetch home again his banished; and the men who married strange wives give their hands and offer a ram for their trespass.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe 'guilty' is the word that opens the door to mercy: the brothers say it at last, the woman says it to the king, and the men who married foreign wives own it with a ram in their hands. Confession is the beginning of the way home, and I hold that God never turns away the man who says he is guilty and brings the offering.
